rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the eight-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. Use a midrange temperature to leave room for selectivity adjustments in either direction.

Only the first pair needs improvement, while the last peak is already within 10 minutes. Raising temperature with the gradient unchanged tests selectivity for that pair and should shorten overall retention.
Injection 2 reached the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method, retaining injection 2 as the benchmark.

Narrowing the organic window makes the 10-minute gradient slightly shallower, which should restore first-pair resolution above 1.5 while remaining faster than injection 2. The lower endpoint is still comfortably above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 4’s slope to test whether initial composition can shorten retention without sacrificing first-pair selectivity. Injection 4 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Test the low-temperature selectivity regime with a steeper gradient: the critical pair may separate in the opposite elution order. The broad endpoint protects against excessive late retention, while the shorter gradient tests a potentially faster route to full resolution.

Raise temperature one step while keeping injection 6’s gradient fixed to test separation of the late three-peak cluster. The first pair has some resolution margin at 25 C, so 30 C may improve the cluster without losing early separation.

Return to the successful high-temperature regime and test a slope between injections 3 and 4, targeting first-pair resolution just above 1.5. The last peak should elute near the gradient endpoint or shortly into the hold, potentially giving a faster maximum-CRF method.

Test whether a substantially steeper gradient breaks up the late three-peak cluster seen at 25 C, offering a faster alternative selectivity regime. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Test whether a shallower gradient restores the first-pair resolution lost when the starting organic fraction was raised in injection 5. This probes an alternative maximum-CRF window with a shorter programmed gradient and ample endpoint strength for the last compound.

Test an intermediate-temperature route to full resolution: 35 C may separate the late cluster, while this shallower gradient protects the early pair. Comparing with injection 4 isolates temperature-dependent selectivity and may identify a second maximum-CRF operating region.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness from injection 11 to bring its first-pair resolution above 1.5 while keeping the last peak near, but likely below, 10 minutes. This tests a second fully resolved temperature regime; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves early-pair selectivity at 35 C while shortening the run. This explores a faster alternative to the low-starting-organic methods, with injection 8 retained as the best confirmed fast method.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 8 to add first-pair resolution margin, with a higher endpoint that keeps the last peak inside the gradient. This targets maximum CRF with an approximately seven-minute elution window.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction combined with a shallower slope can preserve first-pair resolution while advancing the later peaks. This extends the window-shift comparison from injections 5 and 10; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Slightly steepen the slope relative to injection 10 to reduce retention while targeting first-pair resolution just above 1.5. The stronger endpoint keeps all peaks within the gradient; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This seeks a more robust maximum-score alternative, while retaining injection 8 as the fastest fully resolved method.

Test a slope just steeper than injection 8 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary. The last peak should elute slightly earlier, but the first pair’s resolution may fall just below 1.5; injection 8 remains the fallback.

Shorten injection 17 by one gradient-time step to retain maximum CRF with less analysis time and substantial resolution margin. This should balance the early critical pair against the third–fourth pair, whose resolution improved with steeper gradients.

Reduce the slope from injection 16 to give its borderline first pair a larger resolution margin while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes. This targets a maximum-CRF compromise between injection 8’s speed and injection 19’s stronger separation.

Trim injection 19’s gradient window and duration while keeping nearly the same slope, targeting its strong resolution margin with all peaks still inside the gradient. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Test whether shifting the starting composition upward at the slope of injection 12 can lift its borderline early-pair resolution while shortening late retention. This could establish a lower-temperature maximum-CRF alternative; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Slightly flatten injection 22’s gradient to raise its first-pair resolution above 1.5, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes. This targets a lower-temperature maximum-CRF alternative without repeating a method.

Preserve injection 2’s successful gradient slope while trimming the endpoint and programmed duration; all peaks should still elute within the gradient. This targets maximum CRF with more first-pair resolution margin than injection 8, which remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use a slope between injections 24 and 21 to target maximum CRF with greater resolution margin than the fastest method and a last peak near eight minutes. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, and the campaign has already achieved the maximum possible CRF.
